Writing views — the reference

Everything you use while writing a view or widget — the variables the body gets, the Jinja that works in SATOM's strict sandbox (and what does not), inputs, the class kit and tokens, JavaScript in the frame, charts without libraries, and patterns for counting, grouping and joining.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.plugin_studio
📍 WherePlugins → Report Studio → New view / Edit
On this page
  • What the body gets
  • The sandbox rules
  • The toolbox (all verified in SATOM's sandbox)
  • Inputs
  • Styling: the class kit and the tokens
  • JavaScript
  • Views versus widgets
  • Performance

What the body gets#

Name What it is
<key> Each dataset the view declares: <key>.rows (list of dicts), <key>.columns (list of names)
data The same datasets as a dict: data["<key>"], data.<key>
params The inputs: params.<name> (text, or a number for a Number input; "" when empty)

Nothing else exists: no request, no user, no SATOM object, no function that reaches anything. A dataset that failed to load arrives empty (and its error is shown in the preview of SATOM Builder's test runs).

The sandbox rules#

SATOM renders the body in an immutable, strict Jinja sandbox with autoescape on:

Rule Consequence
Strict An undefined name or attribute is an error, not an empty string. Use x \| default("") for something optional.
Immutable list.append, dict.update and every mutating method are refused. Build with filters, or count with namespace.
Sandboxed __class__, __mro__, internal attributes: refused.
Autoescape {{ value }} is HTML-escaped. Never mark data as safe.
first / last of an empty list An error. Check the list first, then take [0].

A render error never breaks SATOM: the frame shows a red Plugin render error card with the message, and publishing is refused until it is fixed.

The toolbox (all verified in SATOM's sandbox)#

{# count #}
{{ server_policies_full.rows | length }}

{# filter: keep / drop rows #}
{% set enabled = server_policies_full.rows | selectattr("status", "equalto", "enable") | list %}
{% set no_waf  = server_policies_full.rows | rejectattr("wpp") | list %}

{# filter on an input (built-in datasets give text) #}
{% set mine = server_policies_full.rows | selectattr("appliance_id", "equalto", params.device) | list %}

{# a device-object dataset gives numbers for ids #}
{% set mine2 = fortiweb_vip.rows | selectattr("appliance_id", "equalto", params.device | int) | list %}

{# sort, take the last #}
{% set ordered = server_policies_full.rows | sort(attribute="policy") %}
{{ (ordered | last).policy if ordered else "" }}

{# group #}
{% for g in server_policies_full.rows | groupby("status") %}
  {{ g.grouper }}: {{ g.list | length }}
{% endfor %}

{# distinct values, joined #}
{{ server_policies_full.rows | map(attribute="device") | unique | join(", ") }}

{# sums and running counts #}
{{ [1, 2, 3] | sum }}
{% set ns = namespace(n=0) %}
{% for p in server_policies_full.rows %}{% if p.traffic_log == "enable" %}{% set ns.n = ns.n + 1 %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}
{{ ns.n }} with traffic log

{# join two datasets #}
{% for pol in fortiweb_server_policy.rows %}
  {% set m = fortiweb_server_pool.rows | selectattr("mkey", "equalto", pol.server_pool) | list %}
  {{ pol.mkey }} → {{ m[0].type if m else "no pool" }}
{% endfor %}

{# numbers from text #}
{{ fleet_counts.rows[0].devices | int + 0 }}

{# JSON for your JavaScript #}
<script type="application/json" id="mydata">{{ server_policies_full.rows | tojson }}</script>

Inputs#

Type The viewer gets params.<name>
Device A list of the devices they may see The device id, as text
Select Your options (value|Label, one per line) The chosen value; an unknown value falls back to the default
Text A text box The text (at most 120 characters)
Number A number box A number, or ""
Date A date picker YYYY-MM-DD

Mark an input required to make the viewer fill it. Inputs never change what SATOM reads: the view filters the rows it received.

Styling: the class kit and the tokens#

The frame brings SATOM's light look. Use the classes — no CSS needed:

Class For
fw-card, fw-card-header, fw-card-title, fw-card-body, fw-card-footer Cards
fw-table (in fw-table-wrapper to scroll) Tables
fw-badge + fw-badge-success / -warning / -danger / -info / -primary / -secondary Status
fw-alert + fw-alert-success / -warning / -danger / -info Messages
btn-fw-primary / -secondary / -outline / -danger, btn-sm Buttons
fw-muted Secondary text

In your own CSS use the tokens, never fixed colours, and the view follows the customer's theme: var(--fw-text-primary), var(--fw-text-secondary), var(--fw-surface), var(--fw-surface-alt), var(--fw-border), var(--fw-accent), var(--fw-radius).

The editor lints the stylesheet: @import, external URLs and position: fixed overlays are refused; low-contrast colours are warned. Full list: Plugin CSS rules.

JavaScript#

Your script runs inside the sandboxed frame:

  • window.pluginData — the datasets (pluginData.<key>.rows);
  • window.pluginParams — the inputs;
  • no network, no cookies, no access to SATOM's page; images and fonts only as data: URIs.

🧪Example — A bar chart without libraries

Body:

<div class="fw-card"><div class="fw-card-header"><h2 class="fw-card-title">Policies per device</h2></div>
<div class="fw-card-body"><div id="bars"></div></div></div>

JavaScript:

const rows = (window.pluginData.server_policies_full || {}).rows || [];
const per = {};
rows.forEach((r) => { per[r.device] = (per[r.device] || 0) + 1; });
const max = Math.max(1, ...Object.values(per));
const box = document.getElementById("bars");
Object.keys(per).sort().forEach((d) => {
  const line = document.createElement("div");
  line.style.cssText = "display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;margin:4px 0";
  const label = document.createElement("span");
  label.textContent = d; label.style.width = "140px";
  const bar = document.createElement("span");
  bar.style.cssText = `display:inline-block;height:14px;background:var(--fw-accent);border-radius:var(--fw-radius);width:${(per[d] / max) * 60}%`;
  const n = document.createElement("span"); n.textContent = per[d];
  line.append(label, bar, n); box.append(line);
});

Use textContent, never innerHTML, for values that come from the data.

Views versus widgets#

Both are built the same way. A widget is meant to be small (a KPI, a short list); a view is a full page. Pick the kind when you create it; it only changes how Custom Views shows it.

Performance#

Each dataset is read at every render, for that viewer. Declare only the datasets you use, prefer the narrow ones (server_policies over server_policies_full, a built-in over a 1,000-row device-object dataset), and let an administrator build an admin_… dataset that totals on the server when you only need totals.
